questions.question_text:
Ravi had \_\_\_\_\_ younger brother who taught at \_\_\_\_\_ university. He was widely regarded as \_\_\_\_\_ honorable man.

Select the option with the correct sequence of articles to fill in the blanks.

options.text: a; a; an
the; an; a
a; an; a
an; an; a

questions.solution_text: The first blank needs 'a' (younger brother – consonant sound). The second blank needs 'an' (university starts with vowel sound 'yu'... wait, actually 'a university' since 'u' sounds like 'yu'). The third blank needs 'an' (honorable – 'h' is silent, starts with vowel sound). So correct is A: a; a; an.

questions.question_text:
"I put the brown paper in my pocket along with the chalks..."

*(From G.K. Chesterton's "A Piece of Chalk")*

Based only on the information provided in the above passage, which one of the following statements is true?

options.text: The author of the passage carries a mirror in his pocket to reflect upon things.
The author of the passage had decided to write a poem on epics.
The pocket-knife is described as the infant of the sword.
Epics are described as too inconvenient to write.

questions.solution_text: The passage explicitly states: 'the pocket-knife, for instance the type of all human tools, the infant of the sword.' So (C) is directly supported by the text.

questions.question_text:
Suppose a program is running on a non-pipelined single processor computer system. The computer is connected to an external device that can interrupt the processor asynchronously. The processor needs to execute the interrupt service routine (ISR) to serve this interrupt. The following steps (not necessarily in order) are taken by the processor when the interrupt arrives:

(i) The processor saves the content of the program counter.

(ii) The program counter is loaded with the start address of the ISR.

(iii) The processor finishes the present instruction.

Which ONE of the following is the CORRECT sequence of steps?

options.text: (iii), (i), (ii)
(i), (iii), (ii)
(i), (ii), (iii)
(iii), (ii), (i)

questions.solution_text: When an interrupt arrives on a non-pipelined processor: first the current instruction must complete (iii), then the PC is saved so we can return later (i), then PC is loaded with ISR start address (ii). Correct order: (iii) → (i) → (ii).

questions.question_text: Consider the following $B^+$ tree with 5 nodes, in which a node can store at most 3 key values. The value 23 is now inserted in the $B^+$ tree. Which of the following options(s) is/are CORRECT?

options.text: None of the nodes will split.
At least one node will split and redistribute.
The total number of nodes will remain same.
The height of the tree will increase.

questions.solution_text: Inserting 23 into the rightmost leaf [20, 21, 22] causes overflow (max 3 keys). The leaf splits. The split propagates upward to the root [6, 12, 19] which also overflows, causing the root to split and the tree height to increase. So (B) and (D) are correct.

questions.question_text: Suppose in a multiprogramming environment, the following C program segment is executed. A process goes into I/O queue whenever an I/O related operation is performed. Assume that there will always be a context switch whenever a process requests for an I/O, and also whenever the process returns from an I/O. The number of times the process will enter the ready queue during its lifetime (not counting the time the process enters the ready queue when it is run initially) is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_. (Answer in integer)
questions.solution_text: I/O operations: 1 `scanf` (input) + 20 `printf` calls (output) = 21 I/O operations. Each I/O causes a context switch out (to I/O queue) and a context switch back (to ready queue). So the process enters the ready queue 21 times after the initial entry.

questions.question_text: The output of the given C program is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_. (Answer in integer)
questions.solution_text: `z` points to `a`. `foo(z, b)` sets `*z = b`, i.e., `a = 25`. So `printf("%d", a)` prints 25.

questions.question_text: Consider a memory system with 1M bytes of main memory and 16K bytes of cache memory. Assume that the processor generates 20-bit memory address, and the cache block size is 16 bytes. If the cache uses direct mapping, how many bits will be required to store all the *tag* values? [Assume memory is byte addressable, $1K = 2^{10}$, $1M = 2^{20}$.]
questions.solution_text: Block offset bits = $\log_2(16) = 4$. Cache lines = $16K / 16 = 1K = 2^{10}$, so index bits = 10. Tag bits = 20 - 10 - 4 = 6. Number of cache lines = $2^{10}$. Total tag storage = $6 \times 2^{10}$ bits.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE while computing *First* and *Follow* during top down parsing by a compiler?

options.text: For a production $A \rightarrow \epsilon$, $\epsilon$ will be added to $First(A)$.
If there is any input right end marker, it will be added to $First(S)$, where $S$ is the start symbol.
For a production $A \rightarrow \epsilon$, $\epsilon$ will be added to $Follow(A)$.
If there is any input right end marker, it will be added to $Follow(S)$, where $S$ is the start symbol.

questions.solution_text: (A) TRUE: $\epsilon \in First(A)$ when $A \rightarrow \epsilon$. (B) FALSE: $ \$ $ (end marker) goes to $Follow(S)$, not $First(S)$. (C) FALSE: $\epsilon$ is never in $Follow$ sets. (D) TRUE: $ \$ $ is always added to $Follow(S)$.

questions.question_text:
Consider a probability distribution given by the density function $P(x)$.
$$P(x) = \begin{cases} Cx^2, & \text{for } 1 \leq x \leq 4 \\ 0, & \text{for } x < 1 \text{ or } x > 4 \end{cases}$$
The probability that $x$ lies between 2 and 3, i.e., $P(2 \leq x \leq 3)$ is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_. (rounded off to three decimal places)
questions.solution_text: First find $C$: $\int_1^4 Cx^2\,dx = C \cdot \frac{x^3}{3}\Big|_1^4 = C \cdot \frac{64-1}{3} = 21C = 1 \Rightarrow C = \frac{1}{21}$. Then $P(2 \leq x \leq 3) = \frac{1}{21}\int_2^3 x^2\,dx = \frac{1}{21} \cdot \frac{27-8}{3} = \frac{19}{63} \approx 0.317$.
